crime_highlights: the accused caused the death of Aspen Pallot by means of manual strangulation
the accused must have applied force to Ms. Pallot's neck for some period of time after Ms. Pallot lost consciousness
His conduct falls at the serious end of the manslaughter spectrum
rationale_highlights: Given the youth of the accused, the presence of some, albeit minimal, Gladue factors, and the unknown element of the role his mental illness played in the offence, I would not sentence Mr. Dey at the upper end of that range
His paternal grandmother, who now suffers from dementia so could not be interviewed for the PSR, is indigenous
note: Gladue factors minimal; court says they lower sentence from upper end of range.

crime_highlights: he sought to groom the children by offering money to the youngest complainant in order to carry out the assaults
it was not a single incident, but rather frequent and ongoing behaviour that occurred in a number of homes and over many months
Mr. P. was an adult in position of trust in the children's homes
he violated that trust and preyed on them
the offences have also had a significant impact on the victims
rationale_highlights: I must at the same time take into account the sentencing regime in place at the time of the offences, the passage of time without reoffending, his aboriginal background, and the systemic factors present which were previously recognized and now found in s. 718(2)(e) of the Code
The court must consider to what extent systemic and background factors related to aboriginal offenders explain the commission of the offence and the moral culpability of the offender
Moral blameworthiness, the foundational principle upon which a fit sentence is based, cannot be determined without considering the offender's family, his background, and his community
note: Court never states explicitly how Gladue factors changed the 18 month sentence.

crime_highlights: Stephen served a crucial role in the plot by driving the vehicle in which the victim was kept for some time
he was not primarily responsible for the beating that occurred in the vehicle, although he did hit the victim at least once
He was active in trying to convince Mr. Houle to sign over his home with threats of violence
rationale_highlights: The relevance of Stephen's Metis heritage is muted
there is no onus on an offender to prove a direct connection between their Aboriginal heritage and the index offence that must be satisfied under s. 718.2(e)
I accept that the Gladue Report still supports a more controlled sentence
Stephen's otherwise strong pro-social behaviour suggests that restorative objectives should be given a greater weight in his case
note: Crime passage lacks victim effects; Gladue weight described as muted but supports controlled sentence.
